name: quarter-hour-block-held-signal
rationale: The signal_block_secs dose curve has a bracket with nothing usable inside it, and today's baseline is the first window in weeks where an interior dose could actually clear the promotion rule. The mechanism (merged as PR #26, h1-block-held-signal) holds the composite constant inside a UTC-aligned block, changing only how often compute_btc_target is consulted -- not the rebalance cadence, threshold, zone mapping or any indicator period. Two doses are on record and both are at the ends: 0 (the baseline, recompute every bar) and 3600, which signal-block-3600-parameter measured on 2026-09-20 at 26 trades against an 88-trade baseline (30%) and was rejected on MIN_TRADE_COUNT_RATIO alone despite clearing both the Sharpe and the drawdown criteria; h6-block-held-signal (21600) was rejected on 2026-09-16. Nothing between 0 and 3600 has ever been measured. 900 is the smaller of the two interior doses this run tests, and it is the one with independent motivation: arXiv:2607.09426 measures a quarter-hour periodicity in crypto futures returns driven by clock-scheduled algorithmic activity, and shirube's block_start anchors its boundaries to the Unix epoch, so signal_block_secs = 900 samples the composite exactly on the UTC quarter-hour marks that paper identifies rather than at an arbitrary phase. This also satisfies the doc's warning rule, which binds this run: today is the seventh consecutive run with a negative sharpe_minus_static_mix (-1.5346 at the promotion capital, -26.67 at 500,000 JPY), so at least one generated hypothesis must target trading cost rather than signal quality, and blocking is a turnover mechanism -- per the doc's sublinearity caveat it must be scored on total_fees_jpy, not on trade count. Two things make the interior dose worth testing now specifically. First, today's primary-capital baseline makes only 16 trades, so MIN_TRADE_COUNT_RATIO needs just 8 -- the floor that rejected every recent turnover hypothesis is unusually easy to clear this run, and a throttle finally gets a fair test. Second, 2026-09-20 established that blocking edges out equal-dose rebalance spacing on fees at 500,000 JPY (12,098 vs 12,886 JPY, -6.1%), so blocking is the better-supported of the two throttle families to spend a dose on.

paper_reference.title: The Quarter-Hour Effect: Periodic Algorithmic Trading and Return Predictability in Cryptocurrency Futures
paper_reference.key_claim: Cryptocurrency futures returns carry a measurable quarter-hour clock periodicity generated by scheduled algorithmic activity, and technical and market-state variables improve out-of-sample forecasts of quarter-hour opening returns -- so high-frequency return models should account for clock-time periodicity rather than treating time as homogeneous.
paper_reference.pros: Same asset class and a horizon shirube actually trades, and it maps onto an existing shirube knob with no code change at all: block_start derives its boundary from the absolute Unix timestamp, so any block_secs dividing 86400 lands on UTC-aligned marks, and 900 puts the composite's refresh exactly on the quarter-hour boundaries the paper identifies. It supplies a reason to prefer 900 over other interior doses that is independent of shirube's own data, which matters because the alternative justification -- 'it is between two tested values' -- is pure interpolation.
paper_reference.cons: The paper studies perpetual futures on offshore venues, not bitFlyer BTC/JPY spot, and its effect is a return-forecasting result at the quarter-hour open rather than a claim that SAMPLING an allocation signal on those marks is better. shirube does not trade the quarter-hour opening return; it holds a composite level constant for 15 minutes, which is a different operation from forecasting that bar. The paper reports no fee or slippage model comparable to shirube's tiered bitFlyer commission, and the periodicity it measures could be an artifact of venue-specific funding and settlement schedules that bitFlyer spot does not share. No number from the paper is used as evidence for a dose or an expected improvement; it motivates the CHOICE of 900 over, say, 1200, and shirube's own holdout backtest decides.
